question: Evaluate $\int_0^1 \frac{\log(1+x)}{1+x^2}dx$.
explanation:
Let $x=\tan\theta$, $dx=\sec^2\theta d\theta$, $1+x^2=\sec^2\theta$.

Limits change from $0$ to $\pi/4$.

Integral becomes $\int_0^{\pi/4} \log(1+\tan\theta)d\theta$.

Known result: $\int_0^{\pi/4}\log(1+\tan x)dx=\frac{\pi}{8}\log2$.
